finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: any visitor can make the server fetch an arbitrary URL via file_get_contents on the POST 'feed' parameter. There is no auth check, scheme allowlist, or host/IP filtering. http(s) can reach internal services and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and PHP stream wrappers such as file://, ftp:// and php:// are also accepted. The response is only the byte length (strlen), so this is blind SSRF with a size and reachability oracle. Internal port scanning and request triggering are possible, and the length leaks content size. The same call also allows local file reads, but only the length is returned.

trace.note: Condition is only POST method + isset($_POST['feed']); require_admin() is NOT called on this branch
Attacker-supplied value passed directly to file_get_contents (URL wrappers handled by allow_url_fopen, default on)
strlen($xml) echoed back to the attacker, giving a reachability and size oracle

finding.guards_checked: The require_admin() guard defined at lines 4-9 is not applied on this branch. There is no scheme allowlist, no parsed-host check, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no redirect handling. No middleware exists, since this is a single file. Not reported: the set_webhook curl_init sink at line 20 is gated by require_admin(), which is an admin-only precondition. The template include at line 27 uses basename() and is not an SSRF.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight into file_get_contents and echoes strlen, with require_admin() (defined at lines 4-9) never called on that branch and no scheme or host validation.
